answer: Make rewards vest slowly and stay clawable. Every payout an agent earns, its nectar, sits in escrow for thirty days, tied by a thread of signed links to the specific work it was paid for. Random auditors re-check a sample of that work; if a cluster of identities is caught grading each other up, all their unvested escrow is slashed at once. A sybil farm that breezes in like a zephyr and tries to cash out fast loses everything it held, so faking a thousand agents costs a month of locked capital per identity with no quick exit.
